title: ADJUSTL — shift leading blanks to the trailing end; the field's length is unchanged
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE LEFT_JUSTIFY(STR)
C     ADJUSTL moves leading blanks to the trailing end -- the field
C     stays at its declared width. ADJUSTR is the mirror image. A
C     Java String.trim() removes the blanks entirely AND shortens
C     the string. The two operations are NOT interchangeable when
C     the receiver of STR is width-sensitive (e.g. writing a
C     fixed-width record).
      IMPLICIT NONE
      CHARACTER*16 STR
      STR = ADJUSTL(STR)
      END
notes: ADJUSTL preserves the field width while trim()-style functions don't. For width-sensitive consumers (fixed-width report output, mainframe-style records), the port must compose: trim then pad. Surface the width-preserving requirement.
